learning_outcomes.text: The student understands and can explain the functioning of a computer network and its individual components and protocols.
The student is able to build a basic physical computer network.
The student cables a physical network with the necessary network equipment and network clients.
The student configures the clients and network equipment.
The student analyzes the operation of the network with various tools.
The student is able to simulate a basic network.
The student builds and configures a network in emulation software.
The student analyzes the operation of the network and inspects network packets.
The student can explain the functioning of the learned protocols based on the simulation.

The student is able to demonstrate and explain the functioning of the computer network. The student has insight into the underlying operation of the computer network and the learned protocols and can answer technical questions about them.
The student is able to clearly document their own knowledge building and the functioning of the network.

syllabus_topics: Structure, components and types of networks
Basic network protocols (ARP, DNS, DHCP, NAT)
assessment_rules: The overall grade is on a 1-20 scale, with Theory counting for 50% and Lab for 50%. If the student scores less than 6/20 for either Theory or Lab, the total for the entire course cannot exceed 9/20. Assignments are in English. Partial transfers of successful sub-results (Theory and Lab) are possible within and across academic years for resits, with the Lab resit being a practical exam.
